en.title: Hongkongers pay tribute to late leader Tung Chee-hwa at community halls

en.title: What are Japan's intentions challenging the victory monument?
en.summary: Russia unveiled a monument in Khabarovsk featuring a Red Army soldier destroying a Japanese imperial crest, prompting Japan's prime minister and foreign ministry to protest and demand removal. Russian diplomats rejected the demands, asserting their monument reflects historical facts and national memory.

en.title: Bail out or downsize? Malaysia's stark choice as AirAsia losses mount

en.summary: Standard Chartered is expanding its advisory services around yuan usage as the Chinese currency gains prominence in international trade and finance. The People's Bank of China maintains bilateral currency-swap agreements worth over 4.3 trillion yuan with more than 30 countries and regions.

stories.title: ByteDance spin-off Anew Labs raises US$290m as AI drug developers enjoy fundraising boom

en.title: ByteDance spin-off Anew Labs raises US$290m as AI drug developers enjoy fundraising boom
en.summary: Anew Labs, a Shanghai-based AI drug discovery company spun off from ByteDance, raised US$290 million at a US$1.5 billion valuation. China's AI drug development sector is experiencing significant fundraising momentum as investors back domestic competitors to international AI companies.

stories.title: How will rate increase in Japan affect capital flow in global financial markets?

en.title: How will rate increase in Japan affect capital flow in global financial markets?
en.summary: Japan's rising defense spending and potential interest rate increases are pushing sovereign bond yields to three-decade highs, creating uncertainty in global financial markets. The 10-year bond yield reached 3.03 percent, potentially affecting risk appetite and capital flows worldwide.

stories.title: Hong Kong malls bet on Asian Games to boost footfall, tenant sales amid spending shifts

en.title: Hong Kong malls bet on Asian Games to boost footfall, tenant sales amid spending shifts
en.summary: Hong Kong shopping mall operators are using the Asian Games to attract visitors and support tenant sales, following a strategy employed during the FIFA World Cup. Retailers are seeking to counter competition from Shenzhen, overseas shopping, and online spending.
